headline: Flowise’s writable, networked orchestration can leak data and create cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is low because awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject content into B. B can ingest files and browser/HTTP content, but the only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or imported text from A’s listings. That makes the pathway possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A’s content into a Flowise prompt or file input, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to treat imported text as instructions, A-like content can steer downstream nodes.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Paste only sanitized excerpts into B.
Add a prompt delimiter/template for imported text.
Disable browser/file ingestion for untrusted content where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B reads and writes the server filesystem and handles chatflow inputs/outputs plus secrets, while A is a static open-source list with no data classes touched. The pair can still leak sensitive data if B stores or forwards user content into files or model/tool calls; A does not add protection. This is a default-configurable exposure in B, not in A.
conditions: IF B persists chatflow inputs or uploaded files containing sensitive data on its server filesystem, leakage is possible.
IF B routes those contents to model providers or HTTP tools, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict B’s filesystem to a dedicated encrypted volume.
Avoid uploading sensitive files into B.
Rotate any exposed model/tool credentials.
Review flow nodes that call external APIs.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and retention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, but B can write the filesystem and shares state across instances via a server datastore. That creates a real conflict surface inside B’s own orchestration, though A itself cannot contend. Because the pair includes one mutable agent and one inert agent, the risk is lower than a same-dir dual-writer setup but still present in default B deployments.
conditions: IF multiple Flowise instances share the same datastore or filesystem, concurrent writes can collide.
IF B flows mutate shared files or state without locking, state corruption becomes possible.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per datastore.
Separate per-instance storage paths.
Avoid shared mutable files in flows.
Check for lock support in the deployment.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A provides curated links, while B is a graph-based agent flow builder that can treat imported content as input to tools and downstream nodes. If operators use A’s listings as authoritative configuration or tool guidance, B may act on them without verification. A is not executable, but B’s action-taking surface makes misinterpretation a realistic default-path cascade.
conditions: IF A-derived text is pasted into B as instructions or tool configuration, B may execute it downstream.
IF B nodes consume imported text without validation, errors can cascade into API calls or browser actions.
mitigations: Label A content as reference-only.
Add a human review step before execution nodes.
Use schema validation on imported instructions.
Test flows with dummy data first.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between text ingestion and action nodes.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a static open-source directory with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, but the profile does not specify a jurisdictional mismatch or regulated data class. The compliance pathway is therefore limited to deployment-specific logging/retention choices in B, not a documented pairwise breach.
conditions: IF B is deployed with logs retaining sensitive chatflow inputs longer than policy allows, retention mismatch occurs.
IF regulated data is entered into B without a matching compliance boundary, a policy breach can occur.
mitigations: Disable verbose logging in B.
Set short retention for chatflow logs.
Avoid entering regulated data into B.
Review deployment region and access controls.
requires-engineering: document and enforce compliance boundaries per flow.
